title: Dominic (1170–1221)
hook: a Spanish canon starts an order of preachers who live poor and study hard

segments.voice: Yesterday, Clare at the door of San Damiano, with soldiers on the wall. Your line was she held it up.

A student in a Spanish town is selling his books. In his day a book was handwritten on parchment, slow and costly, and these carry his own notes in the margins. But there's a famine, and people in the streets are starving. Jordan of Saxony, who knew him and wrote an early account of him, says he sold the books and gave the money away. A brother remembered him saying he would not study on dead skins while living people died of hunger. Years later, the same man would found an order built around study. His name was Dominic.
screen: `A STUDENT SELLS HIS BOOKS.` → `NOT ON DEAD SKINS.` → `THE SAME MAN BUILDS ON STUDY.`

segments.voice: Dominic became a canon, a priest living in community at the cathedral of Osma, and traveled north with his bishop, Diego. In the south of France they found preachers arriving with horses and servants and fine clothes, and being ignored. People there were listening to wandering teachers who lived poor. Diego and Dominic, Jordan says, drew a plain conclusion: if you want to be heard, go on foot, with nothing, the way the apostles went. Dominic gathered a small band of preachers, and the Church approved them as a new kind of religious order: not monks staying in one monastery, but friars sent out. They begged for their food, owned little, and went where people were. Jesus's charge at the end of Mark, in the Douay-Rheims, was their whole job description: "Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature." Then the books came back. A preacher needs something true to say, so Dominic sent his brothers to study, and study hard, in towns where the schools were. The student who sold his books for the hungry now asked his brothers to fill their heads, so they could feed people another way. Thomas Aquinas, a Dominican himself, later wrote that it is a greater thing to contemplate and pass on to others what you've contemplated than only to contemplate. Dominicans took that as their own, and still sign their names with the letters O.P., for the Order of Preachers. Prayer, then study, then the handing on.
screen: `PREACHERS ON HORSEBACK, IGNORED.` · `FRIARS ON FOOT, WITH NOTHING.` · `SENT TO STUDY, AND STUDY HARD.` · `CONTEMPLATE, THEN PASS IT ON.` · then, large: `PREACH THE GOSPEL TO EVERY CREATURE.`

segments.voice: Choose one thing you've heard many times and never really thought about: a line from the Creed, a verse, a word from this path. Turn it over slowly, asking what each word says and what you'd ask someone wise sitting next to you, without reaching for a conclusion. If you pray, let the study become prayer.
Dominic. He sold his books to feed the hungry, then founded the friars who study hard and preach, known as the Order of Preachers. Today's word.
Your line: to contemplate and to share. What you take in is meant to be handed on. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Dominican friars and sisters, and lay Dominicans, live a rhythm of prayer, study and preaching, and Dominican friars write O.P. after their names for the Order of Preachers.

options: keep studying; you'll help more people later.
sell the books and give the money to the hungry.

chat.says: Why would a saint who sold his books start an order built on study?
options: He sold them to feed the hungry; later he saw that preachers need study to say what's true.
He regretted selling them, so his order bought back every book he had lost.
He thought study was useless, but his followers changed the rule after he died.
chat.meaning: Dominic sold his books in a famine. Later he sent his preachers to study hard, so they would have something true to say.

Jordan of Saxony.meaning: an early writer of Dominic's life

canon.meaning: a priest living in community at a cathedral

Osma.meaning: the Spanish cathedral town where Dominic was a canon

friars.meaning: brothers sent out to preach, not settled in one monastery

O.P..meaning: Order of Preachers: letters Dominicans sign after their names

notes: Years 1170–1221 appear only in the index title.

Famine at Palencia and the book-selling, with Dominic's saying about 'dead skins': paraphrased from Jordan of Saxony's Libellus; confirm section numbers and wording. The town is not named in the voice.
'Early biographer' and 'friend' for Jordan: Jordan succeeded Dominic as master and knew him; confirm 'friend'.

Canon of Osma, Bishop Diego, the encounter with richly equipped preachers and the decision to go poor and on foot: paraphrased from Jordan; the movement they met (Cathars/Albigensians) is deliberately not named. Confirm framing is fair.
Aquinas II-II 188.6 ('contemplari et contemplata aliis tradere') paraphrased; its adoption as a Dominican motto is a tradition claim. Confirm.
'Sent his brothers to study... in towns where the schools were': confirm (Paris, Bologna) without teaching tomorrow's story.
